text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.

Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Luna is gone. Luna's card stays face down.
The game is over. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the killer, Gemma the officer, Sol the doctor, Luna the citizen, Terra the citizen.

Sol claimed to be the doctor on day two and named Sonnet as a read, which gave the killers a clear target to push back against. Haiku and Sonnet, the killers, spent the game piling pressure on Gemma and Sol until the votes split and nobody could agree. The turning point came when Sol's reveal drew attention and Sonnet kept Sol under fire, so the tied runoff never resolved and the killers slipped through. Sonnet and Haiku won while Gemma, the officer, was voted out on day one and Terra and Luna were taken at night. Sol, Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Luna and Terra all had regrets, but the killers were never caught.
